question.problem:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $-1$ $0$ $1$
$f(x)$ $0.25$ $0.25$ $0.5$

$y$ $10$ $11$ $12$
$f(y)$ $0.1$ $0.7$ $0.2$

Find $\text{Var}[5X-0.5Y].$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula 

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{X}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 0.25+0\cdot 0.25+1\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.25\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.25+0\cdot 0.25+1\cdot 0.5 \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =0.75-{0.25}^{2} \\  & =0.6875.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{Y}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =10\cdot 0.1+11\cdot 0.7+12\cdot 0.2 \\  & =11.1\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}{y}^{2}\cdot f(y) \\  & =100\cdot 0.1+121\cdot 0.7+144\cdot 0.2 \\  & =123.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =123.5-{11.1}^{2} \\  & =0.29.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[5X-0.5Y] & ={5}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+(-0.5)^{2}\text{Var}[Y] \\  & =25(0.6875)+0.25(0.29) \\  & =17.26.\end{aligned}
$$
